findings.observe_how: If tool is named 'Task': matcher "Agent" never fires. If tool is named 'Agent': the hook runs but L420 immediately prints '{}' because tool_name is 'Agent' not 'Task'. Net: the hook can never inject — registered dead weight executed-or-skipped on every spawn. Latent hazards if revived: path.win32.dirname('C:\\')==='C:\\' so the `while (current !== '/')` loop never terminates when no project marker exists above cwd; PDG slices are fabricated at line 10 when no line is mentioned; the catch-all extractor regex /[`"']?([a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,})[`"']?/g (L130) treats nearly any English word as a code symbol (same pollution class as SEED-13). It also emits `updatedInput` to rewrite the agent prompt — the only hook using the documented modify key, but pointless while unreachable.

findings.title: file-claims (LIVE on every Edit/Write in every project) spawns 2-3 fresh `uv run python` + asyncpg processes per edit with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in the read path, and a DB error in isSessionActive silently converts an ACTIVE peer's lock into a takeover
causal_links: SEED-08 (uv-run startup dominates each spawn)
SEED-12 (getSessionId scheme split feeds the claim identity)
D2b-13 (project+user dual registration would double the spawns if not deduped)
findings.observe_how: file-claims.ts main(): checkFileClaim (1 uv+python+asyncpg spawn, which re-runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on every read, db-utils-pg.ts L613-621) + claimFile (2nd spawn) on every Edit/Write; conflict path adds isSessionActive (3rd spawn). Per SEED-08, uv-run startup is the dominant cost — call it 0.5-2s per spawn, so 1-4s tax per edit. Correctness: on ANY isSessionActive failure (DB down, 3s timeout) it returns false -> file-claims.ts L80-82 'Other session is stale - take over the claim' steals the lock from a genuinely active session — the exact conflict the hook exists to block. Latent landmine: the Python-side default URL in isSessionActive says port 5434 while checkFileClaim/claimFile say 5432 (dead today because runPgQuery always injects CONTINUOUS_CLAUDE_DB_URL, but the first refactor that drops that env hits it). Also TOCTOU: check-then-claim is non-atomic across two processes.
findings.telemetry: SEED-08: warm uv-run latency 13-17s on recall path corroborates the startup tax; runPgQuery timeout is 3000ms per spawn (db-utils-pg.ts L71)

findings.title: smart-search-router ripgrepFallback builds a shell command by string-interpolating the model/content-influenced Grep pattern with only `"` and `$` escaped — cmd.exe metacharacters and bash backticks survive (injection), and the `2>/dev/null` redirect is invalid on cmd.exe so the fallback is broken on Windows anyway
causal_links: reachable from lookupSymbol/tldrSearch on every intercepted Grep whenever the daemon is indexing/unavailable
same file as D2b-05/D2b-06
findings.observe_how: A Grep pattern like `x" & calc & "` breaks out of the double quotes under cmd.exe; `%PATH%` expands inside quotes; under a bash shell backticks execute. The pattern is attacker-influenceable via prompt injection in repo content ('grep for <payload>'). Replace with spawnSync('rg', [pattern, dir, ...]) array args and drop the /dev/null redirect (use stdio:'pipe'). Note the same file's Windows daemon path interpolates the JSON query into a powershell -Command string (daemon-client.ts L570-585) with only single-quote doubling — fragile, same fix class.
findings.telemetry: Fallback triggers whenever daemon response has indexing/unavailable status — i.e., on first Grep in any un-indexed project

findings.observe_how: Read any >3000-byte code file outside the allowlist while the TLDR daemon is up: deny with TLDR context. Follow the message's own advice ('Read <basename>') → denied again identically; a defensive `limit: 200` is also denied (only limit<100 passes); `offset: 0` is falsy so an explicit start-of-file windowed read is denied too. The model burns a round-trip per misleading instruction. Fix: honor any explicit limit/offset, and make the bypass instruction match the actual bypass.

notes: Tool-name evidence chain for D2b-01: agent-recall-injector is the only one of the 10 registered under matcher "Task" (active ~/.claude/settings.json, checked read-only) and it wrote an agent-recall.jsonl row during this very review session (2026-06-10T15:22, session b478f78e), proving the live subagent spawn tool matches "Task". The five matcher-"Agent" hooks therefore cannot fire unless the harness internally aliases Agent<->Task — the one caveat; the decisive probe (spawn Explore, see if denied) is in D2b-01.observe_how. Net effect for D2b as a dimension: of 10 PreToolUse router/injector hooks, 5 are dead registrations, 1 is unreachable under either tool name, 1 (agent-recall) has 0/78 lifetime memory yield, and the 3 that demonstrably act (smart-search-router, tldr-read-enforcer, file-claims) each carry a live defect (S0 junk dir + injection + over-denial; misleading deny copy; per-edit uv spawn tax + fail-open lock takeover). Injection-assembly quality is sharply bimodal: agent-recall's path (sanitizeMemoryContent control-strip/HTML-encode/cap + bus-focus allowlist + data-only wrapper) is the only sanitized one; pre-plan-memory injects raw recall output (1500-char cap only), ralph-template-inject would inject whole template files, pre-tool-knowledge injects raw README/package.json excerpts — none hostile today only because their delivery paths are dead. Active-settings facts (timeouts, matchers, agent-recall-injector presence) come from read-only inspection of C:/Users/david.hayes/.claude/settings.json, which mirrors the repo's .claude/settings.json for the 9 duplicated entries quoted as evidence.
